v4l2-relayd.tagline: Pipes any video source into a virtual webcam device.
v4l2-relayd.full_desc: v4l2-relayd is a small background service that uses GStreamer to relay a video source, a file, a network stream, or another camera, into a v4l2loopback virtual camera device. Once running, other applications (video calls, streaming software) can pick the virtual device up as if it were a regular webcam.
reqs: v4l2loopback kernel module loaded
GStreamer installed

visual-studio-code-bin.tagline: The code editor most developers open first.
visual-studio-code-bin.full_desc: Visual Studio Code is a free code editor from Microsoft with built-in debugging, Git integration, an integrated terminal, and IntelliSense completions, extendable through a marketplace of tens of thousands of extensions covering nearly every language and framework. Recent versions add AI coding agents that can plan and carry out multi-step edits, run commands, and iterate, on top of the traditional editing experience.
visual-studio-code-bin.pricing_note: Free binary; Microsoft's own build under a proprietary (non-OSS) license, distinct from the open-source Code - OSS project
reqs: A GitHub account to use the built-in AI agent features

voxtype-bin.tagline: Hold a key, talk, get text, all on-device.
voxtype-bin.full_desc: Voxtype turns speech into typed text: hold a push-to-talk hotkey, speak, and release, and the transcription is typed at your cursor or copied to the clipboard. Transcription runs locally through engines like Whisper or Parakeet rather than a cloud service, and it can automatically duck your music while you're dictating. It works across GNOME, KDE, Sway, Hyprland, and River.
reqs: Optional GPU (NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm/MIGraphX, or Vulkan) to accelerate transcription; runs on CPU otherwise

walker.tagline: One popup for apps, math, files, and more.
walker.full_desc: Walker is a fast, GTK4-based application launcher for Linux that goes beyond opening apps: type a prefix to do quick math, browse files, run shell commands, search the web, dig through clipboard history, or manage Arch packages, all from the same popup. It's built for tiling Wayland setups like Hyprland and is themed and configured through simple config files.
reqs: Its companion 'Elephant' service running in the background

wayfreeze.tagline: Pauses your screen so you can screenshot it in peace.
wayfreeze.full_desc: wayfreeze is a tiny utility for Wayland compositors that freezes what's currently on screen, a still frame you can then screenshot or annotate without anything shifting underneath you. It supports multiple monitors, fractional scaling, and can hide the cursor or run commands before and after the freeze.
reqs: A wlroots-based compositor supporting the wlr-layer-shell, wlr-screencopy, wp-fractional-scale, and wp-viewporter protocols

xpadneo-dkms.tagline: Makes your Xbox wireless controller feel first-class on Linux, over Bluetooth.
xpadneo-dkms.full_desc: xpadneo is a kernel driver that lets Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, and Xbox Elite Series 2 wireless controllers connect to Linux over Bluetooth with full feature support, not just basic button input. It adds rumble, proportional trigger feedback, battery-level reporting, and paddle button support that the generic in-kernel driver lacks. It started as a student project at fortiss GmbH (affiliated with TU Munich) and is packaged here via DKMS so the kernel module rebuilds automatically across kernel updates.
reqs: A Bluetooth adapter (Bluetooth Low Energy support needed for Xbox Series X|S controllers)
An Xbox wireless controller (One S, Series X|S, or Elite Series 2) to pair

yaru-gnome-shell-theme.tagline: Ubuntu's signature look, for the GNOME Shell chrome around your desktop.
yaru-gnome-shell-theme.full_desc: This package installs the GNOME Shell portion of Yaru, Ubuntu's default desktop theme, styling the top bar, overview, lock screen, and system menus to match Ubuntu's look. It's derived from the official upstream GNOME Shell theme and ships in light and dark variants. Installing it alone gives you Yaru's shell styling without pulling in the full icon or GTK theme.

yaru-gtk-theme.tagline: The GTK widget theme behind Ubuntu's familiar desktop look.
yaru-gtk-theme.full_desc: This is the core GTK2/GTK3 stylesheet of Yaru, Ubuntu's default theme, controlling how buttons, menus, title bars, and other widgets look and feel across GTK applications. It's built on top of upstream Adwaita and ships light and dark variants. This is the largest and most visible piece of the Yaru suite since it affects nearly every application window.

yaru-gtksourceview-theme.tagline: Ubuntu-matching syntax highlighting colors for GTK-based text and code views.
yaru-gtksourceview-theme.full_desc: This package provides a GtkSourceView color scheme matching the Yaru theme, so code editors and text views built on the GtkSourceView library (like GNOME Text Editor or gedit) get syntax highlighting that fits the rest of the Yaru-themed desktop. It's a small, focused piece of the wider Yaru theme suite.

yaru-icon-theme.tagline: The colorful, rounded icon set that defines Ubuntu's visual identity.
yaru-icon-theme.full_desc: Yaru's icon theme provides application, folder, and system icons for the Ubuntu desktop, built from the Unity8 Suru icon set and its Suru successor. It's the component most people recognize as 'the Ubuntu look' — orange folder icons, flat colorful app icons, and a matching cursor theme. It's the largest Yaru sub-package by size since it bundles a large set of icon assets.

yaru-metacity-theme.tagline: Ubuntu-styled window borders and decorations for the Metacity window manager.
yaru-metacity-theme.full_desc: This package brings Yaru's visual style to Metacity, the window manager used in GNOME Flashback and some classic desktop setups, theming window borders, title bars, and controls to match the rest of the Yaru suite. It's a small, targeted component for users running a Metacity-based session rather than modern GNOME Shell.

yaru-session.tagline: The glue package that wires Yaru up as a selectable desktop session.
yaru-session.full_desc: This is a tiny metadata package that registers Yaru as a coherent desktop session/theme option, tying together the GTK, icon, shell, and sound components so a display manager or settings panel can offer 'Yaru' as a single selectable theme. It contains no visual assets itself.

yaru-sound-theme.tagline: The login, notification, and alert sounds that come with Ubuntu.
yaru-sound-theme.full_desc: This package provides Yaru's system sound theme, the audio cues for logging in, notifications, alerts, and other desktop events. It combines sounds from the WoodenBeaver and Touch-Remix projects into one cohesive set matching Ubuntu's default sound design.

yaru-unity-theme.tagline: Yaru's styling for the Unity desktop's launcher and panel.
yaru-unity-theme.full_desc: This package adapts the Yaru theme for the Unity desktop environment, styling Unity's launcher, top panel, and dash to match the rest of the Yaru suite. It's aimed at users still running or reviving a Unity session rather than modern GNOME Shell.

yaru-xfwm4-theme.tagline: Ubuntu's Yaru look, brought to the Xfce window manager.
yaru-xfwm4-theme.full_desc: This package themes xfwm4, the window manager used by Xfce, with Yaru's window borders, title bars, and decorations so an Xfce session can visually match the rest of the Yaru desktop suite. It's for users pairing Xfce with Ubuntu's default theming rather than GNOME.

yay.tagline: The AUR helper that makes pacman feel complete.
yay.full_desc: yay is a command-line helper for Arch Linux that wraps pacman and adds support for the Arch User Repository (AUR). It resolves dependencies, downloads and lets you review PKGBUILDs before building, searches both official repos and the AUR in one command, and can track and update development (-git) packages. It's the de facto standard way Arch and Arch-based distros like Omarchy install community packages that aren't in the official repositories.
reqs: An AUR account (username/password via env vars) only if you want to use its package-voting feature; not needed for normal install/search/update use

yt6801-dkms.tagline: The Linux driver that lets a Motorcomm YT6801 chip actually talk to your network.
yt6801-dkms.full_desc: This package is a DKMS-packaged kernel module for the Motorcomm YT6801, a Gigabit PCIe Ethernet controller chip found in some laptop and desktop motherboards (including certain models this driver was added to Omarchy for). DKMS means the module is automatically rebuilt whenever your kernel updates, so wired networking keeps working across kernel upgrades without manual recompilation. It has no user interface; it just needs to be installed on a machine that actually has this specific ethernet chip.
reqs: Only useful on hardware that actually has a Motorcomm YT6801 Gigabit PCIe Ethernet controller chip
Linux kernel headers installed for DKMS to build against
